title: runtime failure surface and interactive SLA mapper
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: Deliver a unified failure surface and an interactive SLA-mapper UI layer that lets oncall and SREs pivot from high-level symptom to root cause across tracing, metrics and logs. Background: We currently have multiple dashboards and ad-hoc tagging for timeouts, overload and model errors. This ticket scopes the taxonomy standardization, tracing hook attribute enrichment, a lightweight metrics pipeline change to expose new cardinality-safe error metrics, and a Grafana dashboard that maps failure categories to affected SLOs and suggested remediation playbooks. Out of scope: backend retry policy changes, model weights/serving code changes, RBAC access changes for private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: A documented failure taxonomy published on Confluence with canonical keys and example signatures for: TIMEOUT, OVERLOAD, MODEL_ERROR, RUNTIME_EXCEPTION, HTTP_4XX, HTTP_5XX, GRPC_STATUS, KERNEL_OOM.
Tracing hooks instrumented in the runtime to attach failure_reason (enum), queue_time_ms, model_latency_ms and fallback_variant to root spans for inference requests.
A metrics pipeline change that emits cardinality-safe counters and histograms (error_category, region, model_family) to the metrics cluster without high-cardinality tags.
A Grafana dashboard (interactive SLA mapper) that shows top-10 failure slices by p95 latency, error rate, and mapped SLO impact with links to traces and logs.
Alerting runbooks updated: alerts for sudden spike in OVERLOAD or queue_time_ms > configured SLO threshold should link to capacity playbook and autoscaler diagnostics.
End-to-end tests that validate error tagging on a synthetic load test and an integration test that the dashboard links open to sample traces and the associated GitHub runbooks.
Stakeholder sign-off from SRE, Runtime, and Console teams recorded in comments.
technical_notes: Taxonomy decisions: use compact enum keys (TIMEOUT, OVERLOAD, MODEL_ERROR, PROTO_ERR, HTTP_CLIENT, HTTP_SERVER, GRPC_CANCELLED, GRPC_UNAVAILABLE, KERNEL_OOM). Avoid encoding model id or request id in metric labels.

Tracing hook design: attach minimal attributes to the root span and any failure child span: failure_reason, failure_code (http/grpc numeric or internal), queue_time_ms, compute_ms, kv_cache_hit (true/false), model_variant. Use string enums to simplify query language joins.
Sampling: keep trace sampling at current baseline; for spans that get failure_reason != null increase sample rate to 100% for 2 minutes using dynamic sampler to capture post-mortem traces.

Metrics pipeline: add a metricer consumer that translates trace-enriched failure events into metrics via the metrics-ingest service. Use aggregated rollups per minute to avoid cardinality explosion. Emit counters: inference.failures.total{failure_category,region,model_family} and histograms: inference.queue_time_ms, inference.compute_ms.

Logs: enrich structured logs at the request boundary with failure_reason and request_tags. Update log ingestion pipeline (Logstash/Fluent) to route high-severity failure logs to the incidents index and add alerting signals in Kibana.

Dashboard UX: interactive filters should allow slicing by region, customer_tier, model_family. Clicking a failure slice opens a flyout with top traces (sampled), recent related PR numbers, and links to the relevant runbook.

SLO mapping: create a mapping table (console-config) that ties failure categories to SLO buckets (e.g., TIMEOUT -> latency SLO, OVERLOAD -> availability SLO, MODEL_ERROR -> correctness SLO). The dashboard computes estimated SLO breach minutes per slice.
Privacy and PII: ensure enriched spans do not include user-provided prompt text; only include model_id hash and request metadata required for diagnostics.
Backwards compatibility: add feature flag runtime.failure_enrichment_v2 to control rollout for Dedicated/Private tenants.
